comment: Solar wind speeds remain elevated due to ongoing coronal hole effects, but are expected to gradually decline throughout the first forecast interval. The anticipated glancing blow from a coronal mass ejection (CME) that left the Sun on 21st July does not appear to have arrived. It is possible it has missed, but there may still be a slight chance of an arrival today. Geomagnetic conditions are likely to remain mostly QUIET but there is a chance for some ACTIVE periods whilst the solar wind remains above background levels. A filament eruption was observed early this morning, which appears to have an associated CME. There are limited data available for analysis, but early indications suggest there may be an Earth-directed component. It is possible that this could arrive late in the third forecast interval and could enhance geomagnetic activity.
role: independent advisory; score_effect=0 until prospective validation
